title: Easter rehearsal dispute and Irving Mills hiring him
summary: After Armstrong's manager called a rehearsal on Easter Sunday, Brown quit; Irving Mills heard him play Trees at the Cotton Club and hired him for Ellington.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, I don't know that I care to mention too -- I'll tell you, one, Louie came there one time, Louie Armstrong came there with a manager, who I won't name. And I was always pretty independent. And this manager called a rehearsal Easter Sunday afternoon. And that was unheard of as far as I was concerned. I went home to Pasadena, to my mother and father's house, you know, and things, on Easter.
So I said, well, I -- can't you make it some other time? And he was a very peculiar man, this manager that he

had, so he said, "We're going to have it Easter Sunday." And I said, "Well, I don't think I can make it." Well, "That's all right, then. We'll get somebody from the studio." Well, what'd he say that for?

I told him, I said, "Now, you do just that." And I had a contract. Lionel and I had a contract with Sebastian, too. And that was on a Sunday. And so I didn't make the rehearsal. I don't know who they got. To take pictures, that's all he wanted, to take pictures for the next day's paper. So I came on to work, and after that work I went to Sebastian and told him I was through.

Well, "No, we got contracts," and so and so. So Les Hite Height, who at that time was leader of the band, and we got together and talked, and he said, "Oh, well, if he wants to go, let's let him go. We'll let him see the East," and like that. So I quit on a Tuesday, was my last day. After that Tuesday this Irving Mills came in the place, and there again we were doing, as I was doing, a lot of soloing. I had a solo in the show, the floor show. I was playing "Trees." You know, the old religious piece, "Trees." And Donald Novis, who was a singer, also went to Pasadena School with me. He sang a chorus of it and I played behind him, and all that kind of stuff.
And so this Irving Mills was in the audience. So after the show, and things, he called me over. This is Irving Mills, yeah. "Want you to go with Ellington." Well, the

gist of it was, I quit on a Tuesday, and on a Saturday I was on the train, heading East with Ellington's outfit. I'd never -- I'd seen Ellington the couple of times he was out there, but I wasn't particularly -- you know, it's all right.
